extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and publishers (member publications of the Australian Press Council)
extracted.subtask_description: Advisory and binding standards and guidelines for reporting and editorial practice used by the Australian Press Council when considering complaints about member publications. Covers topics from general principles and privacy to topic-specific reporting guidance (e.g., family violence, polls, health, race, advertorials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of General Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's Statements of Principles are binding on all publications which are subject to its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms part of the Standards of Practice and is applied by the Council when considering and adjudicating on complaints about particular instances of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Privacy Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement of Privacy Principles forms part of the Standards of Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside the Statement of General Principles and Specific Standards to guide adjudication of complaints involving privacy-related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Standards of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of Specific Standards of Practice, which apply the two Statements of Principles to particular aspects of media practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Specific Standards operationalise the General and Privacy Principles for particular reporting areas and are binding on print and online publishers that are members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Guidelines (status)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council’s Advisory Guidelines may also be taken into account but are not binding Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Guidelines provide recommended best practice and interpretive guidance for publishers; they inform adjudication though they do not carry the same mandatory status as the Statements and Specific Standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family and Domestic Violence Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction: Family violence is a serious cause of public concern and debate. Reporting on family violence once reflected an earlier social view that family violence was essentially a private, family matter that did not...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasises treating family and domestic violence as a public-interest issue, reporting sensitively and responsibly, avoiding minimisation or private-frame portrayals, and being mindful of victim safety and privacy. (Full guideline expands on language, context, sourcing and harm minimisation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Persons with Diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, and Sex Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reporting about people with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and sex characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises respectful, accurate language and avoidance of discriminatory or sensational coverage; provides specifics on terminology/usage and on avoiding harm to vulnerable individuals or groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Elections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers obligations and best practice for election coverage by newspapers and broadcasters, including accuracy, impartiality, providing context, avoiding misleading interpretation of campaign claims, and how polls and projections should be presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance concerning publication and handling of letters to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers editorial responsibilities for accuracy, fairness, disclosure of conflicts or paid material, distinguishing between opinion and fact, and removing or responding to letters that breach standards (full guideline provides procedural and ethical points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on Opinion Polls
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinion polls are an important source and subject of news stories. Newspapers and broadcasters often commission their own polls to provide information about readers’ views or voters' intentions. Opinion polls can be an effective tool...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on correct presentation and interpretation of poll results: disclose methodology, sample size, margin of error, question wording and timing; avoid over-interpreting or presenting polls as definitive predictions; give context and limitations to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital alteration of images
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline addressing digital alteration of images used in publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires transparency about significant digital alterations, avoidance of misleading or deceptive image manipulation that changes the factual record, and labelling or disclosure where an image has been altered in a way that could affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Asylum seekers', 'illegal immigrants' and entry without a visa
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes that the legal status of people who have entered Australia by boat without a visa is complex and potentially confusing. Their entry is not legally authorised but is not a criminal offence. The Australian Government usually...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises careful and accurate use of terminology: avoid criminalising language, explain legal distinctions and status, and provide context so readers are not misled about legal consequences or social realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Nazi concentration camps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Australian Press Council has received complaints about the terminology used to describe World War Two Nazi death camps that were situated in occupied Poland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides correct and historically accurate terminology when reporting on Holocaust-related subjects; warns against euphemisms or inaccurate labels that can mislead or offend; includes references to adjudications (e.g., May 1999) demonstrating Council practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Advertorials
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Advertorial' is the term for newspaper and magazine content that looks like editorial content but is published under a commercial arrangement between an advertiser, promoter or sponsor of goods and/or services and the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires clear labelling and separation of advertorial/commercial material from independent editorial content so readers can distinguish advertising from journalism; warns against disguising commercial content as editorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: References to Religion and Ethnicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council’s Standards of Practice, particularly the Statement of General Principles, provide the binding standards to which publications must adhere, and to which Council refers when considering complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for accurate, non-discriminatory reporting about religion and ethnicity; avoid stereotyping, gratuitous references, or language likely to vilify groups; exercise care in contextualising religious/ethnic identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Reporting of 'race'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council’s Standards of Practice, particularly the Statement of General Principles, cover accuracy and related obligations when reporting on matters of race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises accuracy, sensitivity and avoidance of inflammatory or dehumanising language; guidance includes how and when to identify race, historic context, and consideration of public interest versus potential harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Drugs and drug addiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council offers the following broad guidelines for newspapers’ consideration when reporting drug-related issues: Responsibly report public debate about drug use and addiction; The harmful effects of any particular drug should not be exaggerated...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises balanced and evidence-based reporting: report public debate responsibly, avoid exaggerating harms, don't sensationalise or glamorise drug use, provide context and authoritative sources, and be mindful of vulnerable audiences. (Full guideline expands these points.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Guideline: Health and medical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council views with concern inadequately researched reports on health and medical matters appearing in the press and in the media as whole. The dangers of exciting unreasonable fears or hopes are far too...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that health and medical reporting be well-researched, rely on credible experts and evidence, avoid creating unreasonable fear or false hope, disclose limitations of studies, and take care when reporting on treatments or medical breakthroughs.
